events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.94)
events.body:
This is a rider-side cancellation: cancelled_by = rider, so the fee can only stand through NS-0's rider branch, which sends an on-demand booking to NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. NS-4 makes a cancellation within 3:00 of matching non-chargeable, and after 3:00 chargeable [F2][NS-4]. The timeline is settled: acceptance 14:05:00, rider cancellation 14:07:55, i.e. 2 min 55 s = 175 s, inside the 3-minute window [F2][NS-4]. The $6.61 on record therefore has no basis and is refundable in full [F2][F5][NS-4].

The driver's no-show route cannot rescue the fee either. NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here" (or platform auto-arrival) with GPS inside the pickup radius, then to wait continuously beyond 3 minutes [F3][F4][NS-1]. No arrival of any kind is recorded: driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null [F3][F4][NS-1]. The closest GPS approach was 2189 m at the moment of cancellation, i.e. never within the 200 m arrival radius [F1][NS-1]. Both NS-1 (i) and (ii) fail, so under NS-2 the $6.61 is refunded in full to the rider [F1][NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's statements do not change this: his 14:06 chat "5 min more, traffic is slow" and his later "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" are consistent with being en route only, and system records (GPS) override statements where they conflict [F8][F10][F1][NS-1]. Traffic and weather records are immaterial, since no exemption is being claimed and none is needed [F11][F12][F13][NS-4].

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after acceptance (14:05:00 → 14:07:55), i.e. within the 3-minute window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable.

The driver never pressed "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null; driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (i) is not satisfied and the fee cannot be justified as a rider no-show.
The driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2189 m at the moment of cancellation — he never entered the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 (ii) fails as well.

RydeX is a non-metered service with a fixed quoted fare and only published add-ons; $6.61 cancellation fee is only valid if NS-0/NS-4 conditions are met, which they are not here, so it must be returned.

The chat is complete and every message is timestamped, and the driver's own words at 14:06 were "5 min more, traffic is slow", confirming he had not yet arrived and was still 5 minutes out when the rider cancelled a minute later; the record is complete, so no G12 referral is needed.
Nothing in the records suggests a safety incident or dangerous-driving allegation, so this is a pure fee dispute decided on the timeline, not a SAFE referral.

weaknesses: The driver may argue the cancellation deprived him of the fare after he had already committed to the trip; the rider's own chat message at 14:05 asking "How long will you be?" (F7) shows she knew he had not arrived, and NS-4 gives no relief for a driver being late (NS-8 is informational only), so the rider's fairness argument carries no clause.

The rider has 1 prior dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern, though profile facts cannot decide the case and the driver's own record is likewise clean (F15).

The record shows only 2 chat messages (F9) and a driver statement (F10) that he "was on my way when the rider cancelled" — the driver may use that statement to argue the ride was progressing, though it is contradicted by the GPS fact that he was 2189 m away (F1).

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching (14:05:00 to 14:07:55), and NS-4 makes cancellations within 3:00 of matching non-chargeable; a refund of the $6.61 on record (F5) therefore rests on the rider's own timing, not on any failure I can disprove.

No arrival confirmation of any kind exists: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and neither a driver tap nor an automatic arrival was recorded (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1(i) and (ii) cannot be established on this record.

The GPS closest approach to the pickup point was 2189 m at 14:07:55, so the NS-1 (ii) element (driver at the pickup location per GPS) fails, the $4.50 driver share was never earned, and the fee is refundable under NS-2 rather than retained.

The driver's 14:06 message ('5 min more, traffic is slow') and his later statement 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F10) are consistent with the GPS only as to being en route, not as to arrival; I do not rely on them to retain any part of the fee.

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, all timestamped, the last before the 14:07:55 cancellation), so the case does not fall into the G12 'incomplete chat' escalation route and the fee outcome can be decided on the system records alone.

The driver's traffic explanation does not rescue the fee: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the window and the only band record (Stevens Road, band 4, 30-39 km/h) is moderate, not severe congestion (band 1/2), while weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

Nothing in this file is a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation: the messages are a timing query and a delay answer (F7, F8); the safety escalation routes should not be engaged, and the driver's clean record (4.0 years, 4.77 rating, 652 trips, 0 disputes upheld in 90 days) is offered only so that no adverse account action follows (F15).

Refunding the $6.61 does not expose the driver to a cancellation-rate sanction in this ruling: NS-3's account-action route is a Ryde mechanism, not a remedy in this dispute, and the driver has no upheld disputes in the last 90 days (F15).

weaknesses: The strongest record fact is against me: F1 shows the driver never came within 200 m of the pickup (closest 2189 m at 14:07:55), so the rider's complaint that 'the driver was nowhere near' is factually true and the $6.61 fee cannot be defended on NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii).

F3 and F4 (no recorded arrival, no 'I'm Here' tap and no platform auto-arrival) are null-field facts that the other side will use to argue the driver never attempted the pickup, weighing toward NS-2 refund with the accompanying NS-2 flag_account consequence for abuse of the waiting/cancellation button.

My own client's chat message F8 ('5 min more, traffic is slow') and statement F10 sit awkwardly with F11/F12/F13 — no incident was recorded and the only band was moderate (30-39 km/h) in fair weather — so any 'traffic' justification cuts against rather than for the driver.

The only point in the driver's favour is timing: F2 shows 2:55 against NS-4's 3:00 line, a 5-second margin that could be lost on rounding; and NS-8 (other operators' ETA rule) is informational and cannot be cited either way.
The driver's 90-day history is clean (F15) but profile facts cannot decide the case, and they do not inoculate my client against a flag_account request arising from the 2189 m GPS reading.

points.response: Agreed on the mechanics: F2 records acceptance at 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 2 min 55 s, inside NS-4's 3:00 no-charge window, and F5 records the $6.61 that must therefore be returned. I do not contest this point.
Accepted: F3 (driver_arrived_at null) and F4 (driver_pressed_here_at null, no automatic arrival) mean NS-1 (i) is not established, so the fee cannot stand under NS-1 or NS-0.

Accepted, and this is my client's core point: F1 fixes the closest approach at 2189 m at 14:07:55, far outside any arrival radius, so NS-1 (ii) fails and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full.

Accepted: the driver's own words (F8, F10) are consistent with being en route but are contradicted by F1 as to being anywhere near the pickup, and system records win over statements, so nothing in them supports keeping any part of the fee.
Agreed: F9 shows a complete, fully timestamped chat (F7, F8), so there is no G12 gap and the outcome is decided on the system records — F1, F2, F3, F4 — which all favour the rider.

Agreed and immaterial to the outcome: F11 (Stevens Road band 4, 30–39 km/h), F12 (no incidents on route) and F13 (fair weather) mean no traffic exemption exists, but traffic is irrelevant here because the fee already fails NS-1 (i) and (ii) on F1/F3/F4.
Agreed that no SAFE clause is engaged: F7 and F8 contain only a timing query and a delay answer, so no escalation is needed; F15 is noted but, as a profile fact, cannot decide the case either way.

Agreed that the driver's cancellation-rate consequences are Ryde's own mechanism, not part of this ruling; I do not seek any account action against the driver in this dispute, which is why my request is a plain refund_full of $6.61 with no flag_account.

I do not contest the rider's own timing arithmetic — 14:05:00 to 14:07:55 is 2 min 55 s (F2) — but NS-4's chargeability line is drawn at 3:00 of matching, not at whether the driver had arrived, so this fact goes only to the fee and not to any finding against the driver.

Conceded as to the fee: driver_pressed_here_at is null and driver_arrived_at is null (F3, F4), so NS-1 (i) is not met and no $4.50 driver share was earned; I ask only that the record show the driver never claimed arrival, which it does.

Conceded as to the fee: the closest approach was 2189 m at 14:07:55 and the driver never entered the 200 m radius (F1), so NS-1 (ii) fails; I note for the account side that this is a failure to reach the pickup, not the NS-2 button-abuse case, since no 'I'm Here' tap was ever pressed (F4).

The $6.61 is chargeable only on NS-0/NS-4 conditions (F2, F5), and since the ride was cancelled 2:55 after matching and no arrival, no-show or completed waiting period exists (F2, F3, F4, F1), the fee must be returned; FARE-1 governs published add-ons generally, but the operative clause on this item is NS-4.

I agree the chat is complete and timestamped (F7, F8, F9) and that no G12 referral is needed; the driver's '5 min more' message (F8) is an honest delay report consistent with the GPS, which is why no account sanction for misrepresentation should follow.

Agreed — nothing in the messages, statement, traffic or weather records reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F7, F8, F10, F12, F13), so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 should not be engaged and this stays a fee dispute.

On the account consequence only: the NS-2 flag_account trigger is a recorded 'I'm Here' tap made while GPS shows the driver away from the pickup; here no tap was recorded at all (F4) and the driver's 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes over 652 trips (F15), so the refund should carry no adverse account action.
